title: Water keeps you alive, so why do diamonds cost more?
body: Adam Smith described the puzzle in 1776: water is essential yet cheap, while diamonds are useless for survival yet expensive. Economists resolved it in the 1870s with marginal utility: prices reflect the value of one more unit, not of all units together. Water is usually plentiful, so an extra litre adds little, while diamonds are scarce, so one more is prized. Lost in a desert, you would rank them very differently.
